method: Manual semantic annotation by cbe-l13 from the 56 question texts and build_assumptions in questions_only.jsonl only (candidates, answers and source not read when labeling). swe_type follows the opening wording of each question (What, How, Why, Where). Layer precedence: design/impact (4) > cross-unit flow (3) > unit behavior (2) > definition location (1); Where does not automatically mean layer 1, and a question that asks for a unit's behavior plus its callers or users, or a value or state traced across functions, is labeled 3. A Why question is labeled 4 when its reason concerns interaction with, or impact on, other components, and 2 when the reason is local to one function. Borderline calls are named in the reason.

labels.reason: Asks why the pause writer must exist before a blow-up-flagged decoder is linked; an ordering constraint between two writers and the chain, so a design reason (borderline 2, since it is one function).
Asks for the order in which the transfer-encoding and content-encoding writers handle body bytes across the whole writer chain; cross-unit flow.
Asks how the writer chain is created during CONNECT and torn down before the real request; lifecycle across several units.

Locates one public function, but also asks for the internal function shared with the MIMEPOST handler and the argument that differs between two call sites in different units; cross-unit (borderline 1/2).
Asks for the algorithm that finds or creates a storage chunk when a number is added to one sparse bitset; unit behavior.
Asks why a reused connection's origin and via-peer must be overwritten, i.e. what would go wrong if the old values stayed; impact and design reason.
Asks how the destination is resolved and then encoded into the SOCKS5 request; spans the resolution choice and the proxy state machine.
Asks what the filters' query callbacks must do so one function can return the address; spans the chain walk and several filters' callbacks (borderline 4, since it is an interface contract).
Asks along which call path, through which filter and based on which buffers the pending-send decision is made; cross-unit call path, not pure location.
Asks why the setup filter discards the whole sub-chain instead of reconnecting the existing filters; design reason about filter state after the connection closed.
Asks at which step the setup-only filters are removed and by which criterion; tracing from connect completion to the removal makes it cross-unit rather than pure location.
Asks why one query branch answers from different state for UDP than for TCP; reason is local to one function (borderline 4).
Asks why the liveness check treats pending input differently for HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2; a protocol-dependent policy spanning the generic check and protocol behavior; design reason.
Asks for the conditions inside one filter's liveness check; unit behavior.
Asks how the tunnel's HTTP version is decided and how that choice becomes part of the filter chain; cross-unit.
Asks how the HTTP/3 attempt's reply signal reaches the racing logic and changes when the HTTP/2 attempt starts; cross-unit signal flow.
Asks how the connection switches to HTTP/2 after a 101 reply and how the original request continues on it; cross-unit flow.
Asks where the concurrency limit comes from, from the reuse check down to the holder of the value; traces one value across several functions.
Asks where each DES key is expanded and which routine then uses it for the response; traces one data step from key setup to its consumer (borderline 2).
Asks for the combined conditions that select the GSSAPI mechanism and how Kerberos availability is determined; spans the SASL decision and an availability probe (borderline 2).
Asks where per-connection state is kept and where it is released in teardown; state lifetime across creation and the teardown path.
Asks under which conditions stored Digest state is dropped when redirects are followed; state lifecycle across redirect handling and auth code (borderline 2).
Asks where a global pointer is set, where it is cleared and what clearing does; state lifecycle across init and cleanup (borderline 2).
Asks which characters one predicate accepts and how the path and query encoders use it; unit behavior plus its users (borderline 2).
Asks what one cleanup function releases and from which places it is invoked; unit behavior plus caller tracing (borderline 2).
Asks which truncation positions one function rejects and what each check prevents; unit behavior.
Asks why the generated program resets the handle between transfers but not after the last one; design reason of the code generator and handle reuse.
Asks how one size-parsing routine turns a fractional value with a unit suffix into bytes; unit behavior of an algorithm.
Asks how a graceful shutdown that cannot finish at once is driven from the first attempt to the final free; multi-step flow across the pool, multi handle and filters.
Asks in which function and file one reference count is incremented; location of a single statement.
Asks for the data structures set up by one init function and the purpose of each; unit-level structure explanation (borderline 3, since purposes show in other pool functions).
Asks where each connection left in a share's pool is shut down and freed when no multi handle exists; flow from share cleanup through pool destruction and shutdown.
Asks why the no_reuse bit is set even on connections that are not closed now; impact and design reason of a network-change policy.
Asks for the conditions under which one comparison treats two origins as the same destination; unit behavior of the matching logic.
Asks which function tells the multi handle which socket events to wait for across two FTP phases; 'by which function' traces the multi-to-protocol hook, so cross-unit (borderline 1).
Asks how one SFTP quote command runs from string parsing through the state machine to the next entry, including a server refusal; multi-state flow.
Asks how a wildcard transfer finds matching files and then downloads them one after another; flow across listing, matching and download steps.

Asks what mechanism carries a failure from state handlers that return libssh codes back through the doing callback to the multi handle; error flow across states (borderline 4, since it is a contract).
Asks why the control connection is closed after a ranged download instead of being kept for reuse; design reason with impact on connection state.
Asks why one function passes block as FALSE to the pingpong state machine; local choice in one function, tied to non-blocking use (borderline 4).
Asks how a random-bytes call reaches a concrete TLS backend, including backend selection when none is set; flow across the multi-SSL dispatch layers.
Asks through which functions the handshake completion time travels to the APPCONNECT timer; call and data path across the TLS filter and progress code.
Asks why the filters, including the TLS backend hook, are not polled when the transfer wants neither send nor receive; design reason spanning the multi handle, the chain and the backend.
Asks for the contract the TLS layer sets for backends that supply channel-binding data; interface contract coupling the layer, its backends and a consumer (borderline 2/3).
Asks which function launches the DoH requests and in which file; pure location of one named responsibility.
Asks how one DNS filter decides whether, when and in what form to print the resolved addresses; logic inside one filter (borderline 3).
Asks how a finished DoH probe response turns into addresses for the waiting transfer; flow across the DoH code, the resolver cache and the transfer.
Asks why every failed lookup becomes a negative cache entry even when the failure may be transient; design tradeoff.
Asks where in lib/ the one decision about storing a Secure cookie over plain http is made; location of one decision point (borderline 2/3).
Asks what one flag in the cookie jar controls inside the cookie engine; unit behavior of one field (borderline 3, since its uses are spread over functions).
Asks through which functions a header travels from response-header parsing to the HSTS store; call path across units.
Asks which ownership rules decide which handle frees the HSTS cache; ownership lifecycle across the easy handle and the share (borderline 4).
Asks why saved TLS sessions are imported through a fresh easy handle with the shared handle attached; design reason about where the session cache lives.
Asks why unbinding from the owning part comes before freeing parts; ordering reason about back-references between objects, i.e. impact if reversed (borderline 2).
Asks how a socket-activity call reaches the affected transfers and returns the next timeout; flow across the socket API, the multi handle and the timer.
Asks where the boundary characters come from; traces a data source from the mime code through the random-byte layers (borderline 2).
